summary: Skagit County two-story smokehouse-style lookout on Butler Hill, built about 1938, on a 1942 Aircraft Warning Service list, and gone by about 1952.

facts.design: Two-story 10 by 10 foot smokehouse-style lookout, per FFLOS and WillhiteWeb
facts.status_note: Destroyed around 1952 per firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; the Register says removed in 1952.

access.note: WillhiteWeb says the land is private; do not go without permission. The area is heavily signed and there is no access at this time.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says removed in 1952; firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb say destroyed around that year. The year agrees.
The Register's build-year text is cut short ('Built in 193'); firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb give 1938.
The Register lists the state Division of Forestry/DNR as administrator; WillhiteWeb lists the landowner as private land.

sources.title: Dr. Quentin C. Belles remembers fire-watching in the '40s

notes_for_editor: Access is set to private from WillhiteWeb, which says permission is needed and there is no access. The 1942 AWS activation is the only staffing evidence; it was a supplemental day-watch post, not a paid lookout. Belles's recollection is hedged by the author himself and is used only as a single sentence. The Register's build year is cut off in the text, so 1938 is taken from firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb.
